First, a steel metal bracket of 4 mm thick is introduced in the high stress region of the seatback. The seatback reinforced with the metal bracket is then analyzed for the combination of all the 7 peak loads as illustrated in Fig. 4.1.5. The stress, strain and resultant displacement contours are shown in Fig. 4.1.5. The maximum resultant displacement is reduced from 11.7 cm in case of fully polymer composite (ABS/CF20) design to 3 cm when 4 mm thick metal bracket is introduced. To further enhance the stiffness of the seatback, a 10 mm thick metal bracket is introduced as shown in Fig. 4.1.6. The maximum resultant displacement is further reduced to 1.7 cm as shown by the contour plots. Figure 4.1.5. Seatback frame design with 10 mm thick metal bracket: (a) Stress map, and (b) Resultant displacement contour Furthermore, the stiffness of various seatback designs is compared in Fig. 4.1.7. The metal frame has the stiffness of 1100 N/m. The fully polymer composite seatbacks have low stiffness of 260-320 N/m, comparatively. Introducing the metal reinforcement though the L-shaped bracket enhanced the stiffness from 320 N/mm to 930 N/mm. However, the stiffness is still less than the metal frame and directly increasing the thickness of the metal bracket will increase the weight. To this end, the seatback with metal reinforced needs to be optimized to minimize the amount of material (i.e., weight of the seatback) while satisfying the performance requirements. Figure 4.1.7. Stiffness comparison for seatback frame: (a) Metal frame design, (b) Fully polymer composite seatback, and (c) Polymer composite seatback with metal reinforcement 4.2 Topology Optimization The fully polymer composite seatback design is optimized using commercially available topology optimization tool, Tosca solids from ABAQUS FE software in this section. A fully polymer composite seatback made up of ABS/CF20 is topology optimized using controller-based optimization. Compliance is used as an objective for this optimization with the material volume as an equality constraint. The optimizer leads to the elements being either void (density very close to zero) or solid (density equal to one) in the final design.
